verdict.reasoning: Patient states breathlessness has been “slowly getting worse over the last couple of weeks” and “become quite troublesome, in the last few days,” and doctor restates “last couple of weeks… but worse in the last couple of days.”

Patient says “normally I can walk to the shops, without a problem but, now I'm having to sort of sit down and catch my breath. And I'm really starting to get a bit breathless, just about the house,” and doctor summarizes “more breathless on kind of minimal… exertion.”
Patient reports “I've got a bit of a dry cough, but it's not too troublesome,” which matches a mild dry cough.
Patient denies chest pain (“No pain in my chest”), palpitations (“No, not really” to palpitations), and fever (“no” to temperatures or fevers).

Patient notes ankle swelling: “my ankles have got a bit bigger… it's sort of swollen up a bit… both ankles… last few days,” and links it to prior heart failure: “I think my ankles did swell up a bit last time, the heart failure was a problem.”
Patient says “I'm feeling a little run-down, um, but otherwise pretty normal” and confirms appetite is fine: “Yeah, I… I'm, that's fine” when asked about eating and drinking.
Regarding urination: patient states “yeah. I usually pee a lot, , ever since the drugs,” referring to diuretics, indicating frequent urination since starting them.

Patient says “I've got um, heart failure” and describes “a small heart attack… About, five years ago… they took me into hospital,” matching history of heart failure and prior small heart attack ~5 years ago.
Patient states “I take something called Furosemide” and when asked dose says “I can't remember,” indicating dose is unknown.
Patient: “I take Aspirin.”
Patient: “And uh, Bisoprolol.” Doctor confirms after clarifying the audio.
On allergies, patient replies “no, no allergies,” and doctor repeats “No.”
Patient: “my father died of a, uh, of a heart attack… he was, um, early sixties.”
Patient: “my mother had osteoporosis.” Doctor asks “Is your mother still with us?” Patient: “yeah, she's still living.”
Patient: “I live on my own. Well, I got two cats… they're called, Polly and Tim.”
Patient: “I work part-time as, a, uh, lorry driver.” When asked about hours: “I only take shifts during the day, I don't like working at night,” supporting day shifts.
Patient says “Not any more” to smoking, then “Yeah” to used to smoke, “about a pack a day… for… good twenty five years,” indicating ex-smoker 1 pack/day for 25 years.
On alcohol, patient states “I don't drink alcohol.”
Patient: “I try and walk to the shops, at least once a day.”

Doctor’s impression: “I wonder whether you've had a flare-up of your heart failure… It seems like your heart's not pumping as well as it should be,” in context of “feeling breathless… worse in the last couple of days” and “some swelling in your ankles,” consistent with suspected heart failure exacerbation with progressive dyspnea and bilateral ankle edema.

Doctor: “I'm quite happy to increase your dose of Furosemide. Maybe, rather than one tablet a day, we can do two tablets a day, for the first few days… increase your Furosemide, uh, to you know, one tablet twice a day.”

Doctor: “let's get a blood test done. We can check your um, you know your full blood count… We can have a check of your kidney function,” which corresponds to ordering FBC and renal function labs today.

Doctor: “maybe doing a couple of other tests, like… an echocardiogram of your heart… That's something I can organize for you today. And… that might take a week or two weeks for that to be organized,” consistent with echo in 1–2 weeks.
Doctor: “I really like, would like you to come back and see me in about a week's time, see how you're getting on.”

Doctor advises: “if you are getting more unwell, feel like you're getting more breathless, or you're having any other symptoms like chest pain, or palpitations or dizziness, then… give me a call sooner.”
Doctor states: “Given that you're otherwise well at the moment, and having examined you, your chest… are all OK,” implying chest exam was okay.
Same sentence: “having examined you, your chest, and your saturations and blood pressure are all OK,” explicitly indicates BP and oxygen saturation were okay.
